lesson: Manual R8 context-pack inclusion produces packs roughly 2× larger than pre-R8 (515 vs 237 lines for WU-003 vs WU-002). Aider-style PageRank/tree-sitter compression planned in ADR-001 §D7 is justified by data, not speculation.
action: Adopt v1.1 context-compiler with Aider-style ranking. Confirm projection with usage data after first 5+ work_units.

lesson: Codex external review caught 3 distinct fix rounds that local self-check missed: wrong Matt Pocock file paths (skill subcategory omitted), wording inconsistency between context-pack intro and Appendix A, and cross-decision contradictions (D1 skip output incompatible with D3 ready_with_override structural requirements).
action: Pre-execution checklist must include explicit fact-check against external state (paths, commit hashes, schema references) and wording-consistency scan between document sections (intro / body / appendices).

lesson: Multi-decision ADRs may contain hidden cross-decision contradictions invisible to per-decision self-check (concrete example: WU-003 D1 specified --skip producing minimal ready_with_override; D3 required ready_with_override to have non-empty unresolved_ambiguities[] and populated override block; both decisions individually well-formed; contradiction visible only when read together).
action: Add cross_decision_consistency field to review_scorecard_template. Reviewer explicitly diff-checks decisions against each other for structural compatibility, particularly when one decision constrains structure (D3) and another invokes it (D1 --skip output).

lesson: First constitution amendment succeeded without changing R1-R17; amendment work_units can safely modify governance when write scope is narrow and diff verification is mandatory.
action: Future constitution amendments must include a textual diff check proving unchanged rules remained unchanged.

lesson: WU-004 showed lessons.jsonl is useful only when context-pack and execution output prove specific influence, not citation.
action: Schemas should add a lessons_applied field or review checklist item for work_units consuming lessons.

lesson: Semantic touching of core rules should count as touching for amendment review requirements, even when existing rule text is unchanged.
action: Schema for amendment work_units should include affects_core_safety_rules and semantic_relations fields.

lesson: Parser/grep-style checks caught a forbidden ellipsis before VERIFIED; simple textual checks prevent governance artifacts from leaking placeholders.
action: Schema verification should require forbidden-pattern checks for markdown governance artifacts, not only YAML/JSON parser validation.

lesson: WU-005 multi-output (primary ADR-003 + 3 secondary schema files) succeeded with conditional gate logic; secondary_artifacts_policy block enables deferral path (D1 GUARD case) without making default gate unsatisfiable.
action: Future multi-output investigation WUs MUST declare secondary_artifacts_policy with deferred_allowed_only_if conditions and explicit if_deferred propagation to gate fields. Single-output WUs are simpler default; opt into multi-output only when secondary artifacts depend on primary's decision.

lesson: WU-005 declared JSON Schema meta-validator gap (ajv/jsonschema unavailable locally) and adopted parser-only validation with deferred validator implementation as a separate OQ. This is the correct pattern when tooling is missing — explicit gap recording + parser+structural fallback + deferred follow-up WU, not silent acceptance of weaker check.
action: Whenever a WU produces format-bound artifacts (JSON Schema, custom DSL, etc.), run validator_tooling_preflight first; if required validator missing, declare gap explicitly in ADR/work_unit notes and create deferred implementation Open Question. Do not pretend full validation.

lesson: WU-005 work-unit-v1 schema initially defined promote_gate.required_pass items as string-only based on author's mental model. Reality (WU-002/003/004) used Hash form ({verification.foo: true}); WU-005 used mixed Hash+String. Codex caught the gap by reading actual yaml files. Schema fix: items.oneOf [string, object].
action: Schema design MUST cross-reference actual existing artifacts (read all instances of the artifact type) before declaring field shapes. Do not encode mental model unchecked. Specifically: enumerate every value/shape that appears across historic instances; pick schema constraint that is union over reality, not narrower.

lesson: ADR-003 D5 lessons-mapping table promised 'verification.rules_unchanged_check encoded in schema if-clause when amendment_class is present', but the schema's then-clause initially required only amendment_target. Cross-decision contradiction was visible only when reading ADR table against schema implementation. Codex caught it.
action: When an ADR contains a mapping table that claims specific schema fields exist or are enforced, the WU verification step MUST cross-check each table row against the actual schema file (or other referenced artifact) before VERIFIED. This is mandatory for ADR-with-secondary-artifact patterns and for memory-stream test traceability.

lesson: AppMaker's durable asset is the harness (governance + workflow + memory layer + verification gates + safety constraints), not any single LLM model. Models change quickly (Opus 4.7 today, Opus 5 tomorrow); the harness is what accumulates value across sessions and projects, and what makes 'less smart model on better harness' beat 'smarter model on weaker harness' for repeatability.
action: Future optimization should target the harness — context construction (R8 + v1.1 compiler), gates (R5 fail-closed + 3-stream logging), traces (events.jsonl audit), review loops (Codex external + self-check), safety constraints (R14 + agent-role.yaml), and pruning (per-project skill activation, archival). Treat 'better model' as one axis among many, not the dominant one. Do not let model excitement substitute for harness work.

lesson: Human understanding, judgment, taste, domain invariants, and trust boundaries cannot be delegated to agents; AppMaker may outsource execution but must preserve human-owned decisions. Specific failure modes prevented: assuming Stripe email = Google email (identity confusion), assuming UI looks 'good' without verification (taste delegation), assuming domain invariants hold without humans naming them (silent assumption inheritance).
action: Future PRD, architecture, and implementation work_units must explicitly mark which assumptions require human judgment and which tasks are agent-executable. PRD specifically must include Understanding section: users/buyers/operators, domain invariants, identity model, trust boundaries, non-delegable human judgments, verifiable success criteria, failure modes / unacceptable outcomes.

lesson: context-pack.md is executable harness logic, not passive documentation. Each context-pack is a Software 3.0 program: it programs the agent's behavior for one work_unit through inclusion/exclusion of context, lessons, decisions, gates. Treating it as 'just briefing' produces drift; treating it as program produces predictability.
action: Context-packs must have schema/checklist/bounds (R8 inclusions, lessons traceability, scope statement, forbidden patterns, self-check). v1.1 context-compiler design must formalize this — context-pack as compilable artifact, not free-form markdown. Future ADR for context-pack schema may emerge when v1.1 work starts.

lesson: If a requirement cannot be verified, AppMaker must either turn it into a verifiable proxy or mark it as human-reviewed. Unverifiable requirements (e.g., 'beautiful UI', 'good UX', 'feels right') silently fail because no gate catches their absence. Verifiable proxies for 'beautiful UI': screenshot review, layout constraints, accessibility checks, user workflow completion. Verifiable proxies for 'feels right': specific user scenarios with success criteria.
action: PRD success_criteria must be verifiable (auto-check OR human-review-with-explicit-criteria). Acceptance criteria for any work_unit must mark each criterion as verifiable. Future ADR-NNN for Verifiability Standards when implementation/UI work surfaces concrete needs; until then, principle informs PRD shape, ADR acceptance criteria, downstream WU verification design.

lesson: WU-006 ADR-004 had D4↔D6 contradiction (D4 required PRD status ACCEPTED but D6 introduced ACCEPTED_WITH_INHERITED_OVERRIDE). cross_decision_consistency review_scorecard field existed in WU-006 contract but was PASSIVE (a label/flag) not ACTIVE (an explicit pairwise diff step). Codex caught the contradiction by reading D4 and D6 together. Lesson #3 from WU-003 already named the failure pattern; WU-006 confirmed that PASSIVE scorecard field is insufficient.
action: cross_decision_consistency MUST be an ACTIVE explicit step in self-check: for each decision pair (D[i], D[j]) where they share concepts (status enum, gate logic, schema field), execute pairwise diff and confirm semantic agreement. Not just a scorecard field name. Future schemas-extension WU may formalize as `verification.cross_decision_consistency_check.pairs` array with explicit pair enumeration.

lesson: WU-006 mapping entry initially had lowercase `accepted_with_inherited_override` while ADR-004 used UPPERCASE. Cross-artifact field-by-field consistency check was missing. Codex caught it by reading mapping entry against ADR-004 simultaneously. Stale-sync after ADR-004 casing decision wasn't propagated to mapping entry (which was drafted earlier).
action: For multi-output WUs, cross-artifact field-by-field consistency check MUST be mandatory verification step BEFORE VERIFIED. Each terminology, status name, field name, or convention claimed in primary artifact must be verified to match in secondary artifacts. Future schemas-extension WU may formalize as `verification.cross_artifact_consistency_check.{primary, secondary}` array of field references to compare.

lesson: WU-006 ADR-004 D4 had internal wording contradiction within a single decision: line 121 said 'AppMaker kernel rejects creation' but line 128 said 'v1 gate is human-enforced; mechanical kernel deferred to ADR-005'. Both claims in same decision text. Codex caught it via sequential read of D4. Pre-promote self-check did not catch because no within-decision line-by-line wording scan was active.
action: Wording-consistency self-check WITHIN each decision (line-by-line internal review for terminology consistency: e.g., kernel vs process vs human; v1 vs v2; mechanical vs human-enforced) MUST be a self-check step distinct from cross-decision check. Particularly for decisions with both 'Decision' and 'How / Implications' subsections — these often diverge during editing and need synchronization.

lesson: events.jsonl correction pattern (retro_recorded_v<n> with `supersedes` pointer to prior entry) has been used 3 times across 4 WUs (WU-003 retro_recorded_v2, WU-005 retro_recorded_v2 + v3). The pattern is stable: append-only-respected, audit-trail-preserved, semantically-clear correction. Time to formalize as schema convention rather than ad-hoc per-WU naming.
action: Future schemas-extension WU should formalize the correction-event pattern: events.jsonl entries gain optional `supersedes` field (string referencing prior event by `<event_name>@<timestamp>`) and optional `_v<n>` suffix on event name. Documented as the canonical pattern for any append-only stream that needs corrections. Constitution R10 (append-only) explicitly allows this — corrections don't violate append-only because they're new entries with explicit supersedence pointer, not history rewrites.

lesson: WU-007 ADR-005 D4 'reserved' a 7-value enum for work_unit_subtype (null|decomposition|review|retro|amendment|interview|prd) — but ADR-005's scope was ONLY decomposition. Reserving the other 5 values silently accepted future taxonomy without dedicated ADR. Codex caught: 'reserved' wording in code blocks counts as acceptance unless explicitly qualified.
action: When defining an enum/field/structure, list ONLY accepted v1 values. Candidates for future expansion go to Open Questions explicitly named 'NOT accepted by this ADR' or 'candidate future X — requires dedicated ADR'. Avoid 'reserved' / 'placeholder' wording in normative blocks because it commits silently. Schema-extension WUs are the only place to introduce new enum values formally.

lesson: WU-007 ADR-005 D4 conflated two distinct WU classes: 'decomposition WU' (the single WU executing the decomposition stage and producing decomposition.md) vs 'materialized slice WUs' (the downstream output set). Annotation `work_unit_subtype: decomposition` was applied to wrong target. Codex caught the cross-decision-internal contradiction.
action: When a field annotates a WU class, decision text must name precisely WHICH class — singular vs plural; producer vs product. Add explicit subsection distinguishing roles when conflation is plausible (e.g., 'X WU' vs 'WUs produced by X'). Per WU-006 lesson within_decision_wording_consistency, this is a within-decision scan target.

lesson: Recurrent across WU-002/003/004/005/007: literal `...` in inline code examples (yaml.safe_load(...), --reason='...', [<slice_id>, ...]). Always self-caught by parser-grep, but pattern repeats across every WU producing markdown with code samples. Cost: pre-VERIFIED grep + manual fix each time.
action: Inline code placeholders MUST use concrete type notation (e.g., `array<slice_id>`) or named placeholder (`<file>`, `<reason>`), NEVER literal three-dot ellipsis. Add as standing rule to context-pack template / executor checklist for any WU producing markdown with code blocks. Future schemas-extension WU may formalize as ADR-v2 schema field forbidden_inline_patterns enforcement.

lesson: WU-007 contract had ACTIVE cross-decision pairs (7) and cross-artifact-consistency fields per WU-006 lessons (schema-level enforcement). Self-check during execution ran them as PASSIVE scorecard markers (annotated 'aligned' without surfacing the diff). Codex caught D4 enum-scope and target-confusion issues at external review by ACTIVELY EXECUTING the pairwise diff. Schema-level field presence is necessary but insufficient — runtime execution of the check is what catches drift.
action: ACTIVE cross-checks must be EXECUTED by executor pre-VERIFIED (run the diff, surface results in §Verification table with explicit aligned/misaligned status per pair), not just annotated as scorecard fields. Future schemas-extension WU may formalize 'verification_commands' for investigation work_units (analog to implementation type) — bash scripts that diff each pair and exit non-zero on misalignment.
